intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous mutation in the STX11 gene (605014) on chromosome 6q24.2.

paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is a form of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis caused by mutation in the gene encoding syntaxin-11. Patients may have fever, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia, together with defective natural killer (NK) cell lysis and degranulation (Muller et al., 2014). Compared with other forms of FHL, the course may be milder, with long remissions without specific treatment. However, some patients have severe psychomotor retardation, and some develop myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myelogenous leukemia (Rudd et al., 2006).

checks.evidence_quote: Linkage of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) type-4 to chromosome 6q24 and identification of mutations in syntaxin 11.
checks.explanation: The paper states that FHL4 is caused by syntaxin 11 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Rudd et al. (2006) studied 6 patients with STX11 mutations from 4 families. Three of the 6 had long periods (1 year or more) of remission without specific treatment, which is very uncommon in FHL. Despite this milder phenotype, some children with STX11 mutations developed severe psychomotor retardation. Two of the 6 patients developed myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myelogenous leukemia, and Rudd et al. (2006) suggested that STX11 mutations may be associated with secondary hematopoietic malignancies.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) described 3 children (2 males and 1 female) from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families who presented with HLH at ages 2 months, 5 years, and 48 months. Patients A and B had fever, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia. Neither had hemophagocytosis or neurologic manifestations. Both were treated with dexamethasone, cyclosporine A, and etoposide and were in remission at 2 months, but both later died. Patient A had undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) at 15 months. Patient C was lost to follow-up. All 3 patients had defective NK cell lysis of K562 target cells and defective NK cell degranulation, both of which IL-2 stimulation partially restored. Expression of perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal, suggesting that granule integrity was intact.

paragraphs.text: zur Stadt et al. (2005) screened positional candidate genes in the large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL linked to 6q24 and identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients homozygous for the deletion. The same homozygous 5-bp deletion was found in 2 additional consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds. In another consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindred, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2). In 2 further consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds, they identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in STX11 that leads to a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein.

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) sequenced UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2 in 3 patients with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families. All 3 carried a novel homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in an alpha-helix of the predicted Habc domain. The parents were heterozygous and had no history of inflammatory disease. Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in cells from 1 patient. In transfected cells, the L58P mutant failed to bind Munc18-2 (see PATHOGENESIS).

paragraphs.text: Muller et al. (2014) found greatly reduced syntaxin-11 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and lymphokine-activated killer (LAK) cells from patient C, who was homozygous for the L58P mutation. Munc18-2 levels in these cells were normal. In transfected HEK293T cells, the L58P mutant and an N-peptide R4A mutant were expressed at wildtype levels but failed to bind Munc18-2, whereas the FHL4-associated Q268X mutant bound normally. The authors concluded that both the N terminus and the Habc domain of syntaxin-11 are required for binding to Munc18-2. They suggested that loss of this interaction destabilizes syntaxin-11 in patient cells.

paragraphs.text: Locatelli et al. (2020) reported an open-label, single-group, phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone to patients aged 18 years or younger with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Of the 34 treated patients, 27 had been previously treated and 7 had not. A response occurred in 63% of previously treated patients and in 65% of all patients who received emapalumab, significantly more than the prespecified null hypothesis of 40%. Seventy percent of previously treated patients went on to transplantation. Emapalumab was not associated with organ toxicity, but severe infections developed in 10 patients, and treatment was stopped in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis. The study concerned primary HLH generally and was not specific to FHL4.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL4 linked to chromosome 6q24, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. The same homozygous deletion was found in 2 additional consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds.

paragraphs.text: In 3 patients with FHL4 from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families, Muller et al. (2014) identified a homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in an alpha-helix of the predicted Habc domain. The parents were heterozygous and had no history of inflammatory disease. Cells from 1 patient showed greatly reduced syntaxin-11 expression with normal Munc18-2 levels. In transfected HEK293T cells, the L58P mutant was expressed at wildtype levels but failed to bind Munc18-2. The authors suggested that loss of this interaction destabilizes syntaxin-11 in patient cells.
